problems.title: Area, perimeter, and radii of a Reuleaux triangle
problems.statement_md: Let $T$ be the intersection of radius-$w$ disks centered at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side $w$. Verify its constant width and compute its perimeter, area, circumradius, and inradius.
problems.hint_md: Decompose the region into the equilateral vertex triangle and three circular segments. Use the common center of the inball and circumcircle for the radii.

figures.caption_md: The incircle and circumcircle share the symmetry center; their radii sum to the width.
figures.alt: Reuleaux triangle with vertex triangle, concentric inscribed and enclosing circles, and labeled radii.

problems.title: Area of a convex circular-arc polygon
problems.statement_md: A convex region is bounded counterclockwise by minor circular arcs joining $v_i$ to $v_{i+1}$, all of radius $r$, with central angles $0<\alpha_i<\pi$. Each arc bulges outside the chord polygon. Prove $A=\frac12\sum_i\det(v_i,v_{i+1})+\frac{r^2}{2}\sum_i(\alpha_i-\sin\alpha_i)$.
problems.hint_md: For each boundary arc, add the sector and subtract the isosceles triangle below it. The remaining central polygon has a shoelace area.

sources.locator: Exercise 2.3(ii), reformulated for arbitrary arc polygons

figures.caption_md: A perturbed and exactly closed unit-edge pentagram gives unequal boundary arc angles. The support lines remain one unit apart.
figures.alt: Irregular five-arc Reuleaux polygon with labeled vertices, chord polygon, and parallel supporting lines.

problems.title: Regular Reuleaux polygons approach the disk
problems.statement_md: For odd $n\geq3$, construct a width-$w$ regular Reuleaux $n$-gon from a regular vertex polygon. Show that its vertex circumradius is $R_n=w/[2\cos(\pi/(2n))]$, its perimeter is $\pi w$, and its area is $A_n=\frac{w^2}{2}[\pi-n\tan(\pi/(2n))]$. Prove $A_n$ increases to $\pi w^2/4$.
problems.hint_md: The longest chord of the regular vertex polygon must have length $w$. After computing the area, study $\tan x/x$ to obtain the monotonicity.

figures.caption_md: Regular Reuleaux polygons of width one; their areas increase toward the disk.
figures.alt: Three equal-width outlines: Reuleaux triangle, regular pentagon, and regular nonagon.

problems.title: The turning-angle budget for disk polygons
problems.statement_md: A convex disk polygon has boundary arcs of radius $r$ and central angles $\alpha_i$, with exterior turning angles $\beta_i$ at its vertices. Prove $\sum_i(\alpha_i+\beta_i)=2\pi$. If it is a Reuleaux polygon of width $r$, show that both sums equal $\pi$.
problems.hint_md: Follow the tangent once around the boundary: it turns continuously on each arc and jumps at every corner.

problems.title: Eroding a disk polygon preserves the centers
problems.statement_md: For $D=\bigcap_i B(c_i,w)$ define $D_{-t}=\{x:x+tB\subset D\}$, where $0\leq t<w$. Prove $D_{-t}=\bigcap_i B(c_i,w-t)$. Explain why the list of active boundary arcs can change as $t$ increases.
problems.hint_md: For a fixed center $c_i$, what is the farthest distance from $c_i$ to a point of $x+tB$?

problems.title: Perimeter and area after eroding a regular Reuleaux polygon
problems.statement_md: For odd $n\geq3$ and width one let $\delta=\pi/(2n)$, $R=1/(2\cos\delta)$ and $0\leq t<1-R$. Set $q=1-t$ and $\alpha=\arcsin(\sin\delta/q)-\delta$. Show that the eroded regular Reuleaux polygon has arc angle $\beta=2\delta-2\alpha$, perimeter $nq\beta$, and vertex radius $r_t=\sqrt{q^2-\sin^2\delta}-R\cos(\pi/n)$. Compute its area by circular segments.
problems.hint_md: Intersect two neighboring circles of radius $1-t$. Their common chord is perpendicular to the line of centers; use the resulting right triangle.

problems.title: Constructing genuinely irregular Reuleaux pentagons
problems.statement_md: Give a concrete construction of a nonregular width-one Reuleaux pentagon. One method is to build an equilateral five-edge star walk $q_0q_1q_2q_3q_4q_0$, reorder its vertices around their convex hull, and intersect the five unit disks. Verify the additional pairwise-distance, convexity and active-arc conditions needed to ensure that the result has constant width. An exact-coordinate example or a perturbation construction with a justified admissible range is acceptable.
problems.hint_md: Keep the first star edge fixed, perturb the next directions, then close the last two edges by intersecting two unit circles. Stay on the branch near the regular configuration.
